questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Difference Between Weather and Climate' refers to.
questions.a: Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, while climate is the average weather condition of a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Difference Between Weather and Climate'.
questions.a: Weather is short-term and changes frequently, whereas climate is long-term and represents the general pattern of weather.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Difference Between Weather and Climate' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Weather and Climate

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Elements of Weather' refers to.
questions.a: The main elements of weather are temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed and direction, and atmospheric pressure, which together describe the state of the atmosphere.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Elements of Weather'.
questions.a: The elements of weather are measured using specific instruments and their values determine the daily weather conditions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Elements of Weather' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Elements of Weather

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Measurement of Temperature' refers to.
questions.a: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of the air, measured using a thermometer in degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F), with maximum and minimum thermometers recording the day's highest and lowest temperatures.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Measurement of Temperature'.
questions.a: Temperature is measured at a standard height in a Stevenson screen to obtain accurate and comparable readings.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Measurement of Temperature' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Measurement of Temperature

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Measurement of Rainfall' refers to.
questions.a: Rainfall is measured using a rain gauge, which collects rainwater and expresses the depth of rainfall in millimetres (mm) or centimetres (cm).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Measurement of Rainfall'.
questions.a: Rainfall is recorded daily at a fixed time, and the monthly and annual totals help understand the climate of a region.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Measurement of Rainfall' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Measurement of Rainfall

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Wind and Atmospheric Pressure' refers to.
questions.a: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air above a place, measured with a barometer; differences in pressure cause wind, which is the horizontal movement of air from high-pressure to low-pressure areas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Wind and Atmospheric Pressure'.
questions.a: Wind always blows from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas, and its speed and direction are measured using an anemometer and a wind vane.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Wind and Atmospheric Pressure' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Wind and Atmospheric Pressure

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Weather Instruments' refers to.
questions.a: Weather is measured using instruments such as the thermometer (temperature), barometer (atmospheric pressure), rain gauge (rainfall), hygrometer (humidity), anemometer (wind speed) and wind vane (wind direction).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Weather Instruments'.
questions.a: Each weather instrument measures a specific element of weather, and together they provide the data for weather records and forecasting.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Weather Instruments' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Weather Instruments

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Weather Forecasting' refers to.
questions.a: Weather forecasting is the prediction of weather conditions for a place and time in the future, based on data from weather stations and satellites.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Weather Forecasting'.
questions.a: Weather forecasts help people prepare for extreme weather and plan activities such as agriculture, aviation and daily life.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Weather Forecasting' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Weather Forecasting

concepts.title: Effect of Weather on Daily Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Effect of Weather on Daily Life' refers to.
questions.a: Weather affects daily life in many ways, influencing clothing, food, housing, occupations, transport and health, and extreme weather can disrupt normal activities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Effect of Weather on Daily Life'.
questions.a: People adapt their clothing, food and daily routines according to the weather, and extreme weather events require special precautions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Effect of Weather on Daily Life' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Effect of Weather on Daily Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Humidity and the Water Cycle' refers to.
questions.a: Humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air, measured as relative humidity using a hygrometer; it plays a key role in evaporation, cloud formation and the water cycle.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Humidity and the Water Cycle'.
questions.a: High humidity reduces evaporation and causes discomfort, while low humidity increases evaporation; humidity is essential for rainfall.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Humidity and the Water Cycle' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Humidity and the Water Cycle
